what_its_for: Pregabalin is used to treat nerve pain caused by conditions like diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury. It is also used to treat fibromyalgia (widespread muscle pain), partial seizures (a type of epilepsy), and anxiety disorder. It works by calming overactive nerve signals in your brain and body.
how_to_take: Take pregabalin exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. If you are taking the liquid form, use the measuring device provided, not a household spoon. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly can cause withdrawal symptoms like headache, nausea, diarrhea, or trouble sleeping.
dosing: Your dose will depend on your condition and how your body responds to the medicine. Most adults start at a low dose (such as 75 mg twice a day or 50 mg three times a day) and the dose may be gradually increased by your doctor. The maximum recommended dose is usually 600 mg per day, split into 2 or 3 doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store pregabalin at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. If you have unused or expired medication, ask your pharmacist about safe disposal options or use a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking pregabalin, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and raise your risk of serious side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that require you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medications that cause drowsiness (such as sleep aids, anxiety medicines, or muscle relaxants) without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, new or worsening depression or anxiety, severe allergic reaction (swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat, hives, or difficulty breathing), unusual changes in mood or behavior, muscle pain or weakness combined with fever or dark urine, blurry or double vision, or swelling of your hands, feet, or legs. Also call your doctor if you notice any increase in seizure activity.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvement in nerve pain within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment. For seizure control and fibromyalgia, it may take a few weeks to see the full benefit. Do not stop taking the medicine even if you feel better — continue taking it as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the side effects of pregabalin, especially dizziness and drowsiness. Use extra caution to avoid falls. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease or are on dialysis, your doctor will likely prescribe a lower dose, since pregabalin is removed from your body through the kidneys. Pregnancy: Pregabalin may harm an unborn baby. Talk to your doctor immediately if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: Pregabalin can pass into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: The safety and effectiveness in children varies by condition — follow your doctor's specific guidance.
